details: 29 Oct, twice in the owner's session (about 14:45 and 15:20 local) Claude Code showed the owner 'UserPromptSubmit hook [python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/lanes.py] timed out after 10s — output discarded. Raise the hook's "timeout" to allow more time.' The owner asked twice what it means. Measured right after, at load 48 on 12 cores: 0.7-0.9 s per run (3 runs), so the slow runs are rare and the cause is not known (a git lock held by a landing or a gate commit, swap while the podman machine held 20 GB, or a slow git call). A hook that runs at every owner message must never block it, and a warning that names an internal file tells the owner nothing (principle 10).
failing_case: On a loaded machine, during a landing or a gate commit, the UserPromptSubmit lanes hook takes over 10 s and Claude Code shows the owner the timeout warning.
pass_cases: a lanes hook run whose git call blocks (a test holding the index lock or a fake slow git) returns within 5 s with one line that the lanes are unknown
a normal run prints the same lanes line as today
a run over 2 s leaves a log line naming the slow step
reason: tests/test_lanes.py:148 test_blocked_git_gives_one_unknown_line passes at head and fails at the queue base (30.2 s not less than 5.0).
findings.summary: The lanes hook sometimes runs past its 10 s limit

details: PLAUSIBLE (traced, not reproduced: needs a landed-feature fixture). main() arms signal.setitimer(ITIMER_REAL, budget) for every event,
work() runs close_landed for PostToolUse with no distinction between reading and writing. relay_queue._git uses subprocess.run, whose
`except: process.kill(); raise` sends SIGKILL to git when the handler's Overrun passes through; git cannot remove its index.lock on
SIGKILL. Before this change Claude Code's 20 s limit could kill the python hook, but the git child ran to its end; now the hook kills
git itself, and 5x sooner. A stale index.lock in the main checkout blocks merges, queue writes and landings: HIGH (fails on ordinary
use, during exactly the landing the item names). Size: 30.
evidence: plugins/front/hooks/lanes.py:99-101 signal.signal(SIGALRM, deadline); signal.setitimer(ITIMER_REAL, budget) for every event
plugins/front/hooks/lanes.py:131 closed = relay_lanes.close_landed(root)  (inside work(), under the timer)
plugins/front/lib/relay_queue.py:822-838 _commit, update-ref wt/queue-<slug>, diff, merge --ff-only, branch -d
failing_case: A feature branch lands (`relay land wt/x`); the PostToolUse lanes hook runs close_landed(root) on a loaded machine (the very case of the
item: "during a landing"). close_landed computes lanes_state, then relay_queue.close_with_evidence -> _land: rev-parse, planner,
_default_rejects, _commit, update-ref wt/queue-<slug>, diff, merge --ff-only (up to 5 tries with 0.2-1 s sleeps), then lanes_state
again. hooks.json gives this hook 20 s; the change arms a 4 s timer for every event. When it fires inside _land, Overrun is raised in
the middle of subprocess.run, which SIGKILLs the git child:
- after update-ref, before merge: wt/queue-<slug> is left behind; the next close says "wt/queue-<slug> exists (relay queue land, or relay doctor)";
- during `git merge --ff-only` in the main checkout: git is SIGKILLed while holding .git/index.lock, so every later git write in the
owner's main checkout fails with "Unable to create index.lock" until someone removes it by hand;
- a close that did land is reported as "Lanes: not known this time" and its "closed <slug>" line is lost.
Should be: a write that started finishes (or is never started); the deadline bounds only the read-only work.
fix_hint: Arm the deadline only around reads: for PostToolUse cancel (or block) SIGALRM while close_landed's relay_queue writes run, or give
PostToolUse its own budget under its 20 s limit and run close_with_evidence with the timer off; better, have close_landed decide the
closes under the deadline and write them after signal.setitimer(..., 0).
pass_cases: 1. PostToolUse landing event, a landed feature item, a fake git that sleeps 6 s on `merge`: the hook finishes the close, the item is done on the default branch, no wt/queue-* branch and no .git/index.lock remain.
2. PostToolUse landing event, git blocked on every call (fake git that never answers): the hook ends within the 20 s limit of hooks.json with the one "not known" line, and no queue write was started.
3. PostToolUse landing event, normal speed, a landed feature: the output holds the "closed <slug> ..." line and the lanes line, as today.
4. UserPromptSubmit with git blocked: still the one "not known" line within 5 s (the existing pass case).
reason: tests/test_lanes.py LanesHookBounds::test_a_landing_close_finishes_its_writes_past_the_deadline passes, fails on pre-fix; blocked-git landing test passes.
findings.summary: the 4 s SIGALRM deadline now also cuts the PostToolUse landing path mid-write: close_landed's queue landing can be killed between update-ref and merge --ff-only

details: CONFIRMED (reproduced). timed() sets _step[0] = step on entry and never restores the outer step on exit, so after a nested git call
returns, _step still names it while the outer "lanes" step goes on into relay_queue._git / cat_batch, which bypass relay_git.git and
are neither bounded by GIT_TIMEOUT_S nor timed. The item's first goal is "find what the lanes hook waits on"; a log that names the
wrong git call sends the next investigation to the wrong place. Size: 15.
evidence: scratchpad/probe/test_probe_step.py (fake git: exec sleep 60 when an argument is "cat-file", else the real git), default budget:
elapsed 4.1, output "Lanes: not known this time ..."
2026-10-29T17:07:29 lanes hook: overrun in git show-ref --verify --quiet took 4.0 s
failing_case: A git that hangs only on `cat-file` (relay_queue.read_queue reads the items through its own _git, not relay_git.git), default budget.
Now the slow log holds:
lanes hook: lanes took 3.0 s
lanes hook: overrun in git show-ref --verify --quiet took 4.0 s
show-ref had already returned; the hang was in cat-file. Should name the step in progress (here "lanes", or the queue read).
fix_hint: Make timed() a stack: save the previous _step[0] and restore it in finally, so the deadline reports the innermost step still running;
optionally time relay_queue's reads (read_queue, _context_with_relay) as their own steps.
pass_cases: 1. Fake git that sleeps on `cat-file` only: the overrun line names "lanes" (or a queue-read step), not a git command that returned.
2. Fake git that sleeps on every call: the overrun line names the first git call ("git rev-parse ..." or "config"), as the step that hung.
3. A git call that took 2.5 s and returned, then a fast run: one line "<that git call> took 2.5 s", no overrun line (as today).
findings.summary: the overrun log names the last git call that finished, not the step that hangs, so it points the diagnosis at the wrong git command

details: CONFIRMED (reproduced). The test passes budget="1" and asserts only the output text; without the timer, relay_config.main_checkout
(5 s timeout) and project_root (5 s) run before the bounded git, and the 2.5 s per-call bound then yields the same line. The default
BUDGET_S = 4.0 is never exercised, so raising it to 9 would also pass. Project rule: a regression test is checked to fail with the
evidence: scratchpad/probe/test_probe_noalarm.py (copy of plugins/front with the setitimer guard set to False):
failing_case: Disable the SIGALRM deadline (hasattr(signal, "setitimer") -> False) in a copy of the hook and run
test_blocked_git_gives_one_unknown_line against it: the hook takes 12.8 s (over the 10 s limit in hooks.json, the bug of the item)
and the test passes. It should fail: the pass case is "returns within 5 s with one line that the lanes are unknown".
fix_hint: Run the blocked case with the default budget and assert time.monotonic() elapsed < 5 around the subprocess; keep budget="1" only for the log test.
pass_cases: 1. Default budget (no RELAY_LANES_HOOK_BUDGET_S), git that never answers: the run ends in under 5 s (asserted on the elapsed time) with exactly the one "not known" line.
2. Same test against the hook with the deadline disabled: fails (over 5 s).
3. Normal run: the lanes line "start: a (fix, ip 90)" as today.
reason: tests/test_lanes.py:154 asserts elapsed < 5.0 at the default budget; fails at the queue base with no deadline (30 s).
findings.summary: the blocked-git test passes with the deadline disabled: it shortens the budget to 1 s and never asserts the 5 s bound

details: PLAUSIBLE, a narrow window. work() prints from inside the timed region; the timer is cancelled only in main()'s finally. Size: 10.
failing_case: The timer expires inside context(event, shown) (json.dump to stdout) near the end of a slow run: a partial object is written, Overrun is
caught, and context(event, UNKNOWN) writes a second object; Claude Code gets invalid JSON. Should be: exactly one JSON object.
fix_hint: Have work() return the text; cancel the timer (setitimer 0) before printing either the lanes line or UNKNOWN.
pass_cases: 1. Overrun before the line is ready: one JSON object with the "not known" text.
2. Normal run: one JSON object with the lanes line.
findings.summary: the deadline can fire while the lanes line is being written, so stdout gets half a JSON object followed by the not-known JSON

details: CONFIRMED by reading; not reached today since every copy lives in the repository. Size: 5.
failing_case: A relay_land.py copy whose root has no plugins/relay/hooks/merge.py at 2 or 4 levels up: HOOK = "merge.py", so `python -I merge.py judge ...`
runs whatever merge.py sits in the process's cwd, or fails naming cwd/merge.py. Before, the error named the expected absolute path.

2. No merge.py found: HOOK is an absolute path that names where it was expected, never a cwd-relative name.
